issue.title: Templates unnecessarily transform `undefined` to `null`
issue.body:
**I'm submitting a ...** (check one with "x") ``` [X] bug report => search github for a similar issue or PR before submitting [ ] feature request [ ] support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question ``` **Current behavior** If you have a template with e.g. `
`, the compiler seems to silently transform the `undefined` into a `null`, which breaks the template if `s` was, in fact, `undefined`. **Expected behavior** `undefined` should be translated as `undefined`, and `null` should stay `null`. **Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions** http://plnkr.co/edit/TVqp0F8IU9RRGxgqW6z5?p=preview (thanks for the template, very helpful). **What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior?** Javascript has always had `undefined` and `null` as separate objects. It makes no sense to combine them in the template language unnecessarily. **Please tell us about your environment:** Fails on plnkr. * **Angular version:** 2.0.X * **Browser:** all * **Language:** all?
